text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Elisabeth Rehn, U.N. Special Human Rights Rapporteur for the former Yugoslavia, is satisfied with status of refugees in Yugoslavia, condemns violence in Kosovo.
- Coalition opposition co-leader Zoran Djindjic visited Bonn where he met German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel.
- Vice President of the Serbian Chamber of Economy Momir Pavlcevic says there should be no delays with structural and ownership changes.
- Student protesting against local election result annulments were stopped by police cordons Sunday night in central Belgrade.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian Renewal Movement leader Vuk Draskovic believes government will not recognize results of municipal elections in which the opposition won a majority.
- Student and opposition protests over annulment of municipal election results are in third month in Belgrade and other cities in Serbia.
- French National Front leader Jean-Marie le Pen arrives in Belgrade on Tuesday to visit Serbian Radical Party. Le Pen's tour will include Pale in Bosnian Serb Republic.
- Democratic Party leader Zoran Djindic said on return from a visit to Bonn that he was assured the European Union would take a unified stand on developments in Serbia.

- How realistic is the government's plan on zero inflation in 1997? Independent economists believe the regime will not allow uncontrolled printing of money, but since it is more afraid of losing power, occasional monetary blows and dosed inflation can be expected.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Black market dinar slump over the New Year holidays was provoked by private shop-owners who turned their holiday earnings into hard currency, says director of confectionary firm Soko Stark Vojislav Djordjevic.
- Yugoslav government presents new report on violation of international war and humanitarian law in territory of former Yugoslavia.
- Ivica Dacic, spokesman for ruling Socialist Party of Serbia, calls on opposition parties to resolve political issues in parliament and not on the streets.
BORBA

- Renewal and establishment of long-term business cooperation with foreign firms is one of main conditions for revival of domestic economy, says president of the Serbian Chamber of Economy Vlajko Stojiljkovic.
- Bor copper mines general manager Ninoslav Cveticanin says he does not expect better results in first half of this year due to international copper production and consumption trends.
